HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
WRIT - C No. - 18764 of 2026
Court No. - 38
HON'BLE SIDDHARTH NANDAN, J.
1. Heard Shri Gautam Baghel, learned counsel for the petitioners, Shri
Nikhil Kumar, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent no.4
and learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents no. 1 to 3.
2. Shri Gautam Baghel, Advocate has submitted that the last elections
were held on 22.03.2025; but however the same was discarded by the
Deputy Registrar vide order dated 15.05.2025; and the same was
subjected to challenge before this Court by way of Writ-C No. 17915 of
2025 and this Court, vide a detailed order dated 01.08.2025, had set aside
the order dated 15.05.2025; and remitted the matter back to the Prescribed
Authority, to take a decision afresh.
3. Since the Court found that respondent no.2, under Section 25 (2) of the
Act, 1860, gave only consideration to some violation of procedure but did
not return any finding or gave conclusions regarding the requirement of
provision under Section 25 (2) of the Act, 1860; and accordingly, the
dispute was referable to the Prescribed Authority under Section 25 (1) of
the Act, 1860.
4. He has further submitted that the said order of this Court was only
placed before the Prescribed Authority on 19.10.2025, after the expiry of
the period of eight weeks, as contemplated in the order; but however, after
receiving a copy of the order, it was incumbent upon the Prescribed
Authority to proceed under Section 25 (1) of the Act, 1860.
5. However, an order was passed on 09.10.2025, directing the parties

concerned to maintain status quo; and thereafter another order was passed
on 27.02.2026 by way of which the petitioners were directed not to take
any policy decision; and since the term of the Committee was expiring,
the election was notified, it was further provided that the election may not
be held.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners has further submitted that they have
taken specific objection that since the reference was not made by 1/4th
members of the Society, therefore, the reference itself was not
maintainable and even otherwise, since the term of the Committee had
already expired on 21.03.2026, therefore, the reference no longer
survives; but without adverting to the said objections, it has merely been
considered in the impugned order that since the orders dated 07.02.2026
and 19.02.2026, have been violated and therefore, the elections which
were held on 22.03.2025, cannot be sustained.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioners has further argued that the said
finding is absolutely perverse and though there is an alternative remedy
provided under Section 25(1)(d) of the Act, 1860, it is not an efficacious
remedy; and also since there was a specific restraint by the Deputy
Registrar for not holding the elections, though the same was notified on
21.02.2026, even the consequential order dated 29.04.2026 passed under
Section 25 (2) of the Act, 1860 cannot be sustained. He has further
submitted that there is no appeal provided against the order dated
29.04.2026 passed under Section 25 (2) of the Act, 1860; and the only
remedy available to the petitioners is by way of approaching this Court,
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent no.4 has submitted that
though in the impugned order dated 24.04.2026, the issues which were
required to be determined under Section 25 (1) of the Act, 1860 have not
been dealt with, but now since the term has already expired and the
petitioners have not held the elections, there is no infirmity in the order
dated 29.04.2026; but as far as the order dated 24.04.2026 is concerned,
he has fairly submitted that it has not been passed, as per the parameters
of Section 25 (1) of the Act, 1860.
9. The learned Standing Counsel also could not point out from the
WRIC No. 18764 of 2026
2

impugned order dated 24.04.2026 that the grounds as required by this
Court's order dated 01.08.2025 passed in Writ-C No. 17915 of 2025, was
not even adverted to; and in view of the aforesaid he submits that the
impugned order may be set aside and the matter be remitted back to the
Prescribed Authority for fresh determination, to which learned counsel for
the respondent no.4 also does not object. For ready reference, the
operative portion of the impugned order dated 24.04.2026 is being
reproduced below:
"मेरे द्वारा दोनों पक्षों के  िवद्वान अिधवक्ताओं की ओर से प्रस्तुत बहस व साक्ष्यों का
अवलोकन िकया गया। उपरोक्त िदये गये तथ्यों से स्पष्ट है िक प्रितवादी द्वारा िडप्टी
रिजस्ट्रार के  आदेश की िनरंतर अवहेलना की गयी है। िदनांक 19.02.2026 को
यथािस्थित बनाये रखे एवं िकसी भी प्रकार की िनितगत सलाह/िनणर्य न करने के
सम्बन्ध में स्थगन आदेश पािरत िकया गया था िकन्तु इसके  बावजूद भी प्रितवादीगण
द्वारा िदनांक 19.02.2026 को चुनाव सिमित गठन हेतु सभा आयोिजत की गयी।
िदनांक 22.03.2025 को सम्पन्न िववािदत िनवार्चन में अंशधािरता प्रमाण पत्रों का
िवतरण में उपबन्धों का उल्लंघन िकया गया है। िडप्टी रिजस्ट्रार के  पत्र िदनांक
07.02.2026 के  द्वारा वाद का िनस्तारण िविहत प्रािधकारी द्वारा होने तक कायर्कारणी
के  िनितगत एवं बडे िवत्तीय िनणर्यों पर रोक लगायी गयी थी परन्तु प्रितवादीगण द्वारा
उक्त आदेशों की अवहेलना की गयी है। इस प्रकार उपरोक्त तथ्यों के  आलोक में अनेक
अिनयिमत्ताएँ  िनवार्चन िदनांक 22.03.2025 में पायी गयी है। ऐसी िस्थित में वादी का
वाद स्वीकार करना न्यायोिचत प्रतीत होता है।
आदेश
अतः उपरोक्त तथ्यों के  दृिष्टगत वादी का वाद स्वीकार कर सोसायटी का चुनाव िदनांक
22.03.2025 िनरस्त िकया जाता है। उक्त आदेश की प्रित िडप्टी रिजस्टार महोदय,
फम्रस, सोसायटी एवं िचट्स, गािजयाबाद को इस िनदेर्श के  साथ प्रेिषत िक संस्था/
सिमित की कायर्कािरणी गठन के  सम्बन्ध में िनवार्चन हेतु िनयमानुसार कायर्वाही
कराना सुिनिश्चत करें। इस न्यायालय की पत्रावली बाद आवश्यक कायर्वाही दािखल
दफ्तर हो।"
10. This Court finds that the objection relating to the maintainability of
the reference under Section 25 (1) of the Act, 1860 was specifically raised
by the petitioners and it was also recorded in the impugned order; but the
impugned order has been passed without adverting to the requirements of
Section 25(1) of the Act 1860 and as desired by this court in its order
passed in Writ-C No. 17195 of 2025, dated 01.08.2025; and further the
manner in which the elections held on 22.03.2025 has been discarded,
shocks the conscious of this Court, as any subsequent event cannot
invalidate an election, which was held in the year 2025; and as such by
WRIC No. 18764 of 2026
3

non-consideration of the grounds taken by the petitioner, the impugned
order is liable to be set aside on the grounds of violation of principles of
natural justice and the same being absolutely perverse.
11. The court is also conscious of the fact that there is an alternative
remedy provided under Section 25 (1) (d) of the Act, 1860, but in view of
the admission of the learned Standing Counsel and learned counsel
appearing on behalf of respondent no.4 that the issues raised was never
adverted to by the Prescribed Authority, this Court finds that in the given
circumstances, the present writ petition cannot be dismissed on the
ground of alternative remedy, as there is admitted violation of the
principles of natural justice. Accordingly, the order dated 24.04.2026 is
hereby set aside.
12. I have also perused the impugned order dated 29.04.2026 and the
Deputy Registrar has merely observed that since the election dated
22.03.2026 has been set aside and the elections have also not taken place,
while the term of Committee of Management has expired, therefore,
elections can be held, invoking the provisions of 25 (2) of the Act, 1860.
13. At this juncture, Shri Gautam Baghel, Advocate has relied upon
Clause 26 of the model Bye-laws of the society. For the sake of
convenience, the same is reproduced below:
“26. Election and term of office -
(i) The annual general meeting of the Association, to be held in the
first quarter of each financial year, shall elect neither less than 4, nor
more than 10 Members including the President, Vice President,
Secretary and Treasurer from M embers of the Association. Provided
that no member shall be eligible for election if he has been found guilty
of misusing the post during his previous term. The term of office of the
office-bearers of the Board shall be one year from the date of assuming
office and they will be eligible for re-election. Provided that a person
can not hold the same post continuously for more than 2 years.
•
(ii) An arrangement shall be made by the board to ensure that one
third of members of the board retire annually.
•
(iii) The office bearers shall hold office until their successors have •
WRIC No. 18764 of 2026
4

been elected and hold their first meeting.”
14. Perusal of the aforesaid bye-laws, which has been duly approved by
the Authority concerned; specifically under Clause 26 (iii), it has been
provided that the office bearers shall hold office until their successors
have been elected and hold their first meeting. Since the elections were
notified on 21.02.2026, but could not be held on account of an order dated
23.02.2026; it cannot be said that the elections have not been proceeded
with and therefore, now the election is to be held invoking the provisions
of Section 25 (2) of the Act, 1860.
15. In view of the aforesaid, this Court finds it appropriate to relegate the
matter to the Prescribed Authority to examine whether reference which
was made under Section 25 (1) of the Act, 1860 was made in accordance
with law, and to proceed only in case it is found that the reference was
made to it by at least 1/4th members of the Society.
16. The aforesaid decision is to be taken within a period of one month,
from the date of production of a certified copy of this order; whereafter
the election of the Committee of Management shall be held accordingly,
within a period of one month from the date of decision of the Prescribed
Authority, under Section 25(1) of the Act, 1860.
17. With the aforesaid observations and directions, the writ petition stands
disposed off.
May 13, 2026
Sumit K.
WRIC No. 18764 of 2026
5
(Siddharth Nandan,J.)

2. In view of the fact stated in the application, the application is allowed.
3. In the 2nd line of 4th paragraph of the order dated 13.05.2026,  date
"19.10.2025" shall be read as "09.10.2025"; in the 3rd line of 5th
paragraph, date "27.02.2026" shall be read as "07.02.2026"; and in the
3rd line of 12th paragraph, date "22.03.2026" shall be read as
"22.03.2025".
May 20, 2026
